overview: This bill, the No Waivers for Fraud Act, changes the Child Care and Development Block Grant program, the main federal program that gives states money to help low-income families pay for child care. When a state breaks the program's rules, the Department of Health and Human Services can impose penalties, such as withholding some funding. Current law lets the department waive certain penalties; this bill removes that power to waive sanctions, so penalties imposed on states for noncompliance would stay in place. As of April 6, 2026, a House committee had approved it and it was placed on the House calendar.
for: Supporters say penalties only work if they stick, and removing waivers ensures states face real consequences for failing to follow the rules.
against: Critics say removing all flexibility could leave the department unable to ease penalties in unusual situations, such as disasters, where cutting funds would mainly hurt families who need child care.
